unchecked_sentences.text: Creatinine also enters the gate, with a weight of -0.032 per sd; switching that edge off moves the AUC from 0.8883 to 0.8882, so creatinine plays no real part here.

Shape (self-probe: the typical patient with sodium swept in steps of one mmol/L, smoker and non-smoker): for a non-smoker the first exit is off at sodium 133 and on at 132 (value 0.29), growing as sodium falls (value 2.01 at 128); for a smoker it is already on at 134 (value 0.20) and off at 135.
Smoking therefore raises the sodium level at which the gate opens and makes it open wider (value 2.78 for a smoker against 2.01 for a non-smoker at sodium 128).
The second exit opens deeper: at 131 and below for a non-smoker and at 132 and below for a smoker.
Through this part, the typical non-smoker at sodium 128 gets 5.77 added to the logit and the typical smoker 9.02.
In the whole model the typical non-smoker's predicted risk is 14% at sodium 136 and 99% at 128; the typical smoker's is 24% and above 99%.

On the training data the gate is open for 124 patients (67 non-smokers and 57 smokers), whose outcome rate is 67.7% and mean predicted risk 66.2%; the second exit is open for 66 patients (outcome rate 80.3%).
The closed form (analytical_formula evidence) reproduces the part to within 0.017 on the training rows (coefficients rounded).

Concept probe: serum sodium predicts the gate with score 0.99 (meaningful); a U-shaped concept (squared distance of sodium from the middle of its range) scored 0.93, because this part is only the low arm of the model's U in sodium (the high arm is the high-sodium hinges).
Self-probe (typical patient, sodium swept one mmol/L at a time): both exits are off at sodium 139 and on at 140 (values 0.09 and 0.22), rising to 1.57 and 2.74 at sodium 150.
Both exits raise the predicted risk (output weights 1.96 and 1.99): in the whole model the typical patient's predicted risk is 9% at sodium 139, 80% at 145 and 99% at 150.
The noise column enters the first hinge with a weight of 0.224 per sd: for the typical patient with sodium set to 145, the predicted risk is 62% with noise at -2 sd and 90% at 2 sd.
On the training data the second hinge is on for 635 patients (outcome rate 52.4%, mean predicted risk 52.5%); the 75 training patients with sodium > 145 have an outcome rate of 98.7%.
The closed form (analytical_formula evidence) reproduces the part to within 0.0067 on the training rows.

The low-sodium gate (low arm) and the high-sodium hinges (high arm) sit side by side and their output terms are added on the logit; sodium's direct edge (weight -0.631 per sd, in direct_terms) tilts the U slightly downwards with rising sodium.
For the typical non-smoker the low arm is off from sodium 133 upwards and the high arm is off up to 139, so the bottom of the U lies between the two.

The training data follow the same U: the 94 patients with sodium < 133 have an outcome rate of 74.5%, the 739 with sodium >= 137 and sodium <= 141 29.6%, and the 75 with sodium > 145 98.7%.

The heart-rate effect turns over between 120 mmHg (1% slow against 53% fast) and 140 mmHg (34% slow against 3% fast).

Whole model: the output terms of the parts are added with the output bias on the logit scale and passed through the sigmoid; the decomposition reproduces the evolved network to within 1.1e-15 on the training rows.
Sex has no edge in the network and is a zero-effect entry: the typical patient's predicted risk is 9% as female and 9% as male.
